judgments.proposedConclusion: No. DUSD provides the holder an enforceable right to redeem for US dollars with the issuer, failing criterion (b). It is accounted for as a financial asset, not under ASC 350-60.
judgments.question: Does DUSD meet the ASC 350-60-15-1 criteria?

alternatives.notes: Rejected: the maturity leg of the definition is not met; a conclusion of cash equivalent would need to overcome the Practice Aid view and be owned by the reviewer.

judgments.basis: ASC 230-10-20 (cash equivalents: short-term, highly liquid, readily convertible, so near maturity that value changes are insignificant — a stablecoin has no maturity); ASC 305-10-20 cash; AICPA Digital Assets Practice Aid stablecoin Q&A; terms 4.1, 4.2, 5.1; reserve attestation.
judgments.proposedConclusion: A financial asset: a receivable-like contractual right to receive 1 USD per token from the issuer on demand, carried at par with an ASC 326 credit loss assessment. Not cash (the issuer is not a depository institution and the token is not a demand deposit) and not a cash equivalent: DUSD has no maturity, so it cannot meet the ASC 230-10-20 short-maturity test however liquid it is — the AICPA Digital Assets Practice Aid view is that stablecoins are generally not cash equivalents. DemoCo's direct par redemption right settling T+1 and the attested reserves support par measurement and a nil allowance, not a cash-equivalent caption.
judgments.question: Is DUSD cash, a cash equivalent, or another financial asset?

alternatives.notes: Rejected: no contractual right to receive cash exists.

judgments.basis: ASC 350-60-15-1 criteria all met; protocol documentation confirms no redemption right.
judgments.proposedConclusion: ASC 350-60 crypto asset measured at fair value: it is an intangible on a distributed ledger, secured cryptographically, fungible, not created by DemoCo, and conveys no enforceable rights.
